readingInstruction: Read Mark 15:21-47. The march to Golgotha, the crucifixion, the cry of dereliction, the death, the tearing of the temple curtain, and the centurion’s confession. This is the climax of Mark’s Gospel. Read slowly.
settingTheScene: Jesus is led out to Golgotha, the place of the skull. Mark’s account is stark. There is no mention of the forgiveness of enemies or the promise to the thief, which Luke records. Instead, Mark gives us the one cry from the cross: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” Everything in the Gospel has been moving to this point, and the first human to name Jesus rightly at the cross is a Roman soldier.
observation: “And they compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross” (15:21).
“And the inscription of the charge against him read, The King of the Jews” (15:26).
“He saved others; he cannot save himself” (15:31).
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (15:34).
“And Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed his last” (15:37).
“And the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom” (15:38).
“Truly this man was the Son of God!” (15:39).
“Joseph of Arimathea, taking courage, went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus” (15:43).
interpretation:
A passerby, Simon of Cyrene, is forced to carry the cross. Mark names his sons, Alexander and Rufus, probably because they were known in the church. Rufus may be the one Paul greets in Romans 16:13. They offer Jesus wine mixed with myrrh, and he refuses it. They crucify him at the third hour, nine in the morning, and divide his garments. Above him is written, “The King of the Jews.” Two robbers are crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.

Passersby mock him: “Aha! You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself!” The chief priests and scribes say, “He saved others; he cannot save himself.” They speak more truth than they know. He cannot save himself and save us. Even the robbers revile him.

At the sixth hour, noon, darkness comes over the whole land until the ninth hour. Then Jesus cries with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?”, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” This is Psalm 22:1. In this moment, the Son bears the curse of sin and experiences the abandonment that sinners deserve. It is the deepest mystery of the cross. The Father did not abandon him because of anything he did, but because of what he bore. Some bystanders think he is calling Elijah. Someone fills a sponge with sour wine, and Jesus gives a loud cry and breathes his last.

The curtain of the temple is torn in two from top to bottom. This is the curtain between the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place. God himself tears it from the top. Access to God’s presence is now open through the death of Jesus.

Then the centurion, standing in front of Jesus, sees how he died and says, “Truly this man was the Son of God!” The first to confess him as the Son of God at the cross is a Gentile soldier, one of those who had mocked him. This is the high point of Mark. The book began, “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” The secrecy is over. It is at the cross that we see who he really is.

Women, including Mary Magdalene, are watching from afar, and Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council who was looking for the kingdom of God, boldly asks for the body and lays it in a tomb cut out of rock. The women see where he is laid.
connection: Psalm 22 is the psalm Jesus quotes, and it ends in praise and triumph. Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bore our griefs and was pierced for our transgressions. Amos 8:9 foretold darkness at noon. Exodus 26:31-35 and Hebrews 9:8 and 10:19-20 explain the curtain. Galatians 3:13 says Christ became a curse for us. 2 Corinthians 5:21 says God made him to be sin for us. Mark 1:1 and 1:11 echo with 15:39. Romans 16:13 mentions Rufus.
application:
Sit with the cry “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” Thank him that he was forsaken so that you never need to be.

Confess with the centurion, “Truly this man was the Son of God.” Say it aloud.

Consider the torn curtain and approach God today, boldly, because of what Jesus has done.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for being forsaken so you never will be.
Thank him for bearing the curse and the wrath.
Say with the centurion who you believe Jesus is.
